abstract.t:
OAuth 2.0 provides mechanisms for requesting and granting access, constraining access tokens, and managing their lifecycle. It does not define a common way to identify the work a user approved and to associate that work's bounds and termination with the credentials issued for it. When an AI agent acts on a user's behalf, that work is what most needs governing: the agent's authority should come from the approval of a bounded piece of work, should stay within the bounds the user approved, and should end when the work is done or the user withdraws it.
This document presents a use case in which a user withdraws an agent's approved work and the agent's further operations are denied, and identifies the semantics that independently implemented clients, Authorization Servers, and Resource Servers need to share to deliver that outcome. It then describes a framework for approved bounded work, built on three objects: a bounded work proposal, the governing authorization established when it is approved, and approval evidence, a durable record of the authorization decision and the approved bounds. Credentials issued for the work are associated with the governing authorization, and ending the authorization has defined consequences for further issuance and, within a stated acceptance window, for resource access.
This version specifies no wire formats and requests no IANA actions. It is a direction-setting document: its goal is agreement on the problem and the conceptual model, with details left to subsequent revisions and working group discussion.
